title: Local Pet Services: Find Trusted Pet Businesses
description: How to find recommended local pet businesses: groomers, dog walkers, pet sitters, kennels, catteries, vets and independent pet shops, and what to check.
cardText: Groomers, walkers, sitters, kennels, vets and independent pet shops near you.
h1: Local pet services: how to find businesses you can trust
intro: From independent pet shops to groomers and home boarders, good local pet businesses are worth their weight in treats. Here’s how to find them, and what to check before you hand over your pet.

image.alt: Four dogs on leads out on a walk in the park

items.title: Independent pet shops
items.text: Local advice, refill stations and specialist foods. Many offer loyalty cards and local delivery.

items.title: Vets
items.text: Use official finders and check practice accreditation before you register.

blocks.title: Five checks before you book any pet service

items.title: Licence
items.text: Where one is needed (for example, home boarders and kennels in England), ask to see it.

items.title: Insurance
items.text: Ask whether they hold public liability and care, custody and control cover.

items.title: Reviews and references
items.text: Read recent reviews on more than one site, and ask for references.

items.title: A visit first
items.text: Meet them, see the premises and watch how they handle your pet.

items.title: Emergency plan
items.text: Ask how they’d reach you and your vet if something went wrong.

sections.h2: Independent pet shops and local suppliers
sections.html:
Local pet shops, feed merchants, aquatic centres and pet bakeries often stock specialist foods, give hands-on fitting for harnesses and carriers, and can order things in. When comparing them with online stores, look at:

  • Price per day for your regular food, including any loyalty scheme
  • Local delivery or click-and-collect
  • Refill stations and bulk buys for litter, hay and bird seed
  • Expert advice for small pets, fish and reptiles

• UK: use the RCVS Find a Vet search. Practices in the RCVS Practice Standards Scheme are inspected against set standards.
  • US: AAHA-accredited hospitals are evaluated against the American Animal Hospital Association’s standards.
  • Cats: look for a Cat Friendly Clinic accredited by International Cat Care.
  • Ask about out-of-hours emergency cover, health plans and how they share estimates.

We’re building a list of recommended local pet suppliers and services across the US, UK and Europe. If you run a pet business, or know one that deserves a mention, get in touch. Listings will be clearly labelled, and we never publish reviews we haven’t verified.

faqs.q: Do dog groomers need a licence?
faqs.a: In the UK, dog grooming isn’t licensed, so look for qualifications, insurance and good reviews. In the US, requirements vary by state and city.

faqs.q: Do home dog boarders need a licence?
faqs.a: In England, yes. Home boarding, kennels, catteries and dog day care need a licence from the local council, which gives a star rating from 1 to 5.
